inline.s: This is the miracle. Behind every apparently “bad” or “evil” event, person, or situation, there lies a deeper “good.” Through your inner acceptance of what is in this present moment, this deeper “good” reveals itself to you from within. “Do not resist evil” is one of the highest truths of humanity.
“I really can’t do it. I feel agitated and angry about this.”
“Accept that I feel agitated and angry now? Accept my inability to accept?”
“Yes. Bring acceptance into your non-acceptance. Bring surrender into your non-surrender. Then see what happens.”

Chronic physical pain is one of the strictest teachers you can encounter. What it teaches you is this: resistance is futile. Nothing is more common than the “unwillingness to suffer.” Yet, if you can set aside this unwillingness and allow the pain to be there, you may notice that you separate subtly from the pain, that a gap opens between you and it, and that this gap has always existed. This means suffering consciously and willingly. When you suffer consciously, physical pain can quickly burn up your ego, because the ego is to a great extent composed of resistance. This is also true of severe physical disability. To “offer your pain to God” is another way of speaking this truth. You do not have to be a Christian to grasp the profound cosmic truth contained in the symbol of the cross. The cross is an instrument of torture. It represents the greatest pain, limitation, and helplessness that a person can encounter. Then, suddenly, that person bears the pain willingly, with full awareness, expressing it through these words: “Not my will, but thy will be done.” In that moment the cross, the instrument of torture, reveals its hidden face. At once it is a sacred symbol, a symbol of the divine. The cross, which seems to deny that any transcendent dimension exists in life, becomes, through surrender, the gateway to that dimension.
